label: Third original token after a sequence opening "n v" or "v v"
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely at step t=2, when the first two original tokens are n,v or v,v (so the second token is v). It does not depend on L or on what token is at t=2, except that input c gives much higher activation: n v c reaches the max of 1.457. Openings with n v are stronger than v v (v v p is about 0.28 of max, n v plus another token is about 0.35-0.39). It never fires in the delimiter or copy phases. A small amount of weak activation (about 3% of mass) falls on near-miss contexts: other first tokens followed by v then c (k v c, w v c at 0.01-0.08), n n c, and t=3 after n n v / u v v followed by c. On dev the predicate has no false positives.

issues: The factual claims hold on dev. The feature fires only in the original phase (0 activations at the delimiter or in the copy phase). 99.5% of activation mass is at t=2 and 0.5% at t=3. prev_tok=v carries 98.9% of mass, and prev2_tok in {n, v} carries 98.6%. Top examples are all 'n v [c:1.00]'. v v p is about 0.28 of max and n v plus a non-c token is about 0.34-0.39, as claimed.

Test misses (157 steps, 3.3% of mass) are systematic, not scattered: they are almost all a weak tail of input c at t=2 after v or n with some other first token. Coverage of the lowest activation quartile is only 0.52. The explanation describes this tail, but its list is incomplete. It leaves out 'v n c' (0.14) and 'a v c' (0.20, stronger than the k v c / w v c range of 0.01-0.08 it quotes).

Patching the tail gains little. Adding 'a v c' gives test P=1.0, R=0.893, F1=0.944. A broader c-tail clause gives F1=0.952 but drops precision to 0.97. On its own, c after v/n at t=2 has precision of only 0.15-0.23, so c is a magnitude modulator, not a separate trigger. The main predicate stays the right description.
The label ('third original token after a sequence opening n v or v v') matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
